topology: Integration guide keyed by authorization use case: Server-to-Server uses account_credentials with the account ID and no separate refresh flow (request a new token after the one-hour expiry), General uses the user authorization code flow with Local Test page installation; every step shows full HTTP examples including the Base64 basic-auth header, JSON responses with expires_in and scope, plus deauthorization and PKCE sections.
traversal: Use-case sections via on-page outline (request, refresh, revoke, use, me context, deauthorization, PKCE).
responsiveBehavior: HTTP examples scroll horizontally; outline collapses on mobile.
visualWorld: Meeting-platform docs where token lifecycle rules (one-hour expiry, no refresh flow for server apps) are stated as plainly as the happy path.
strengths: Complete request and response pairs are shown, including header construction
The no-refresh-flow rule for server-to-server is stated explicitly, preventing a common wrong assumption
Re-authorization triggers (scope or webhook changes) are documented where the authorization flow is taught
weaknesses: App-type taxonomy (Server-to-Server, General) assumes marketplace knowledge
Rivet library note adds a parallel abstraction without explaining when to prefer it
transferableDecisions: Key OAuth docs by app type with complete request-response pairs
State token-expiry and refresh rules (or their absence) explicitly
rightsNote: Text notes and canonical link only; page extract cached locally, not committed.

title: Twilio Verify API Documentation
firstScreenJob: List nine verification channels, then walk a three-step OTP workflow with samples in nine languages.
topology: API guide: channel inventory (SMS, Passkeys, Silent Network Auth, automatic channel selection, Voice, WhatsApp, Email, TOTP, Push), base URL with HTTPS-only enforcement, authentication guidance preferring API keys in production and Account SID for local testing, then a numbered OTP workflow where each step ships code in Node.js, Python, C#, Java, Go, PHP, Ruby, twilio-cli, and curl, plus annotated JSON responses (psd2_enabled, skip_sms_to_landlines).
traversal: Workflow steps with per-language tabs; advanced features (custom codes, rate limiting, PSD2) linked from the workflow.
responsiveBehavior: Language tabs collapse into a selector on mobile; View as Markdown travels with the page.
visualWorld: Communications-platform docs where production versus local-testing credentials are distinguished before the first request.
strengths: Credential guidance separates production (API keys) from local testing (Account SID) up front
Nine-language code parity per step respects diverse stacks
Response fields are annotated with compliance flags (PSD2) that most guides skip
weaknesses: Nine channels without a selection guide leaves the choice under-supported
Advanced features scatter across links rather than an in-page decision path
transferableDecisions: Separate production and testing credential guidance before the first code sample
Annotate response fields with compliance meanings
